newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Former top European Commission official dies.
newsitem.headline: Former top European Commission official dies.

text.p: Emile Noel, a Frenchman who was the European Commission's top civil servant for almost 30 years, died on Saturday near Viareggio, Italy, officials said on Monday.

Noel, who headed the Commission from 1958 to 1987, was 73. An official at the European University Institute in Florence, where Noel held a post until 1993, told Reuters that he had died at his summer house but she did not know the cause.
"Europe is in mourning," Commission president Jacques Santer said in a telegram to Noel's wife that was distributed to reporters.

Noel began as executive secretary of the Commission when it was the executive body for the just-established European Economic Community uniting Belgium, France, Germany, Italy, Luxembourg and the Netherlands.
He was named secretary general in 1968 after the Commission's role was expanded to cover the activities of what was then known as the European Community -- now the European Union of 15 members.
